summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex bariatric surgical history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by marginal ulcers and later open reversal) was admitted for recurrent acute-on-chronic left upper quadrant/epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the left flank with nausea and early postprandial fullness. Evaluation showed stable vital signs and reassuring labs without evidence of acute infection or surgical abdomen; chest radiograph showed no free air. Bariatric surgery evaluated her and recommended no surgical intervention. She was managed conservatively with a non-narcotic pain regimen (scheduled acetaminophen and continuation of home gabapentin), resumption/continuation of ulcer-directed therapy (pantoprazole, ranitidine, sucralfate), and bowel regimen adjustments. She developed diarrhea during the stay; C. difficile PCR was negative and she was treated symptomatically with PRN loperamide. Given chronic diplopia with negative outpatient EMG for myasthenia gravis and concern for GI side effects, pyridostigmine was discontinued. Symptoms improved and she was discharged home ambulatory without narcotics with referral to chronic pain management for suspected postoperative visceral hyperalgesia and instructions to continue her GI and chronic medications.
problems: Acute on chronic abdominal pain (LUQ/epigastric), suspected postoperative visceral hyperalgesia
Diarrhea (C. difficile PCR negative), treated symptomatically
History of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass status post open reversal; history of marginal ulcers requiring acid suppression
Diplopia with negative outpatient EMG for myasthenia gravis; pyridostigmine discontinued due to GI side effects
Hypotension/dizziness likely related to poor intake/diarrhea during admission
